notes: Espresso-station 5S, tied to the spaghetti finding that earned it a place on this project: Marcus walks ~796 m per peak in the current layout, and route R2 alone -- espresso to grinder and back -- runs 52 round trips per peak, so the station's physical order is part of how the morning runs, not housekeeping for the binder. Three rounds so far (biweekly while the habit forms, then monthly per the schedule), each with a photo the scores can be checked against (photos are the demo's stdlib-rendered stand-ins, same convention as measure/floorplan.png -- plain zlib/struct PNG writing, placement seeded with random.Random(23); the generation run is recorded in control-run.md). The trend is the honest line: 10 to 15 to 18 of 25, improving because the photos changed, not because scoring relaxed -- and nothing is a 5 yet: Sustain has two on-schedule rounds behind it and no more, and Standardize still has a migrating home (the dial-in log). Set-in-order moves land directly on named waste: the pitcher rack beside the wand kills the cross-walkway reach, the grinder shadow board and staged cups shorten the R2 dosing trips, and the cleared walkway removes the crossing where the July 28 rush pileup happened. Every round's lowest category carries an action with an owner; the round-2 low (Sustain) is exactly the category this phase's 6% statistic predicts, and the fix was to chain the audit to an existing Friday routine rather than to good intentions.
